title: Thornbury Castle
text: Begun by Edward Stafford, 3rd Duke of Buckingham, in about 1510–11 beside the parish church of St Mary. More a grand Tudor country house than a fortress, with only a show of defence. Work stopped when the Duke was executed for treason in 1521.
check: Wikipedia gives both 1510 and 1511 for the start.

title: The gatehouse range
text: A symmetrical entrance front with a central gatehouse and octagonal corner towers, in dressed Cotswold ashlar, with crenellations and machicolations. The ornate brick chimneys are among the finest of the period; one is dated 1514.

title: Thornbury Castle today
text: Grade I listed. Kenneth Bell ran it as a restaurant from 1966 to 1986; it is now a 26-room hotel and wedding venue.

title: St Mary's Church
text: The castle was built right beside Thornbury's parish church of St Mary, whose tower gives a view down into the castle courts.
